subject: geography
title: Fluvial Geomorphology and River Landforms
explanation: Fluvial processes involve hydraulic action, abrasion, attrition, and solution that erode bedrock and sediment, with the transport capacity determined by velocity, discharge, and sediment load characteristics. The Hjulstrom curve demonstrates the relationship between particle size and the velocity required for erosion, transportation, and deposition, explaining why rivers create specific landform assemblages in different course sections.
points: Upper course features include V-shaped valleys formed by vertical erosion, waterfalls created at resistant rock bands with plunge pools beneath, and interlocking spurs where rivers wind around valley obstacles before achieving sufficient power to erode through them

Middle course landforms encompass meanders with river cliffs on outer banks where erosion concentrates and point bars on inner banks where deposition occurs, plus oxbow lakes formed when meander necks are cut through during floods

Lower course characteristics include floodplains built by lateral migration and overbank deposition, levees formed by immediate deposition of coarse sediment during floods, and deltas where sediment accumulates as river velocity decreases entering standing water bodies.
